descriptionChirho: The formative training of character through teaching, guidance, and habituation in wisdom and righteousness — the primary sense in Proverbs and wisdom literature.
Corrective punishment or reproof administered to reform behavior, emphasizing the punitive or rebuking aspect of discipline rather than its didactic content.
The content of what is taught or learned, pure teaching or doctrine apart from the corrective aspect, as indicated by Arabic تعليم rather than تأديب.
A physical or metaphorical fetter, bond, or yoke of restraint, derived from the binding sense of the root יסר (as in Jeremiah 5:5).
A cautionary message or admonition intended to avert wrongdoing, distinct from corrective punishment after the fact.
